skill.name: fastapi-pro
skill.description: Build high-performance async APIs with FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2.0, and Pydantic V2. Master microservices, WebSockets, and modern Python async patterns.
skill.summary: Build production FastAPI services with async patterns, data layers, security, testing, and deployment guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a Markdown inline code span on SKILL.md line 24. It references a resource file and does not execute commands, so I marked it false positive. No semantic security findings were added.

static_findings.snippet: - If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 24 uses backticks only as Markdown formatting around a resource path. There is no executable code or command invocation in this prompt-only skill.

content.value_statement: FastAPI teams often need consistent guidance for async APIs, data layers, security, testing, and deployment. This skill provides structured FastAPI architecture and implementation support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Guides FastAPI 0.100+ projects with Annotated types, dependency injection, and OpenAPI documentation.
Designs async data layers with SQLAlchemy 2.0, Alembic, Redis, and repository patterns.
Plans authentication, authorization, CORS, security headers, and rate limiting for APIs.
Creates testing strategies with pytest, pytest-asyncio, TestClient, mocks, and coverage.
Recommends performance, observability, deployment, and integration patterns for production services.
limitations: It provides guidance and generated plans, not direct runtime validation.
It needs project requirements, data models, and deployment targets for precise advice.
Generated examples still require local testing, review, and security validation.
It is scoped to FastAPI and related Python API architecture.

use_cases.title: Launch an Async API
use_cases.description: Plan endpoints, Pydantic models, dependencies, tests, and deployment steps for a new FastAPI service.

use_cases.title: Modernize Data Access
use_cases.description: Move synchronous database patterns toward async SQLAlchemy 2.0, migrations, pooling, and repository boundaries.

use_cases.title: Harden Production Services
use_cases.description: Review authentication, authorization, rate limiting, headers, logging, and observability choices before release.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic API Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use fastapi-pro to outline a simple FastAPI service for [domain]. Include endpoints, Pydantic models, dependencies, tests, and local verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add Async Database Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Use fastapi-pro to design async SQLAlchemy 2.0 access for [entities]. Include sessions, migrations, repositories, pooling, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Secure a Production API
prompt_templates.prompt: Use fastapi-pro to review this FastAPI architecture for authentication, authorization, CORS, rate limits, validation, and security headers: [architecture].

prompt_templates.title: Design a Scalable Microservice
prompt_templates.prompt: Use fastapi-pro to design a production microservice for [workflow]. Include caching, observability, background work, deployment, scaling, and failure handling.

output_examples.input: Design a FastAPI service for customer orders.
output: API contract with order, customer, and status resources.
Pydantic model plan for request validation and response serialization.
Async database strategy with migrations, sessions, and test coverage.
Deployment checklist for Docker, health checks, and OpenAPI review.

output_examples.input: Review my API for production security.
output: CORS, rate limiting, and security header recommendations.
Input validation and SQL injection prevention notes.
Testing and monitoring actions before release.
Likely bottlenecks across queries, serialization, and external calls.
Async pooling and eager loading recommendations.
Caching and pagination options with tradeoffs.

best_practices: Share expected traffic, data stores, authentication needs, and deployment constraints before asking for architecture advice.
Request tests, error handling, and observability plans with every generated endpoint design.
Validate generated guidance against your FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, and infrastructure versions.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a full production system without requirements, data boundaries, or success criteria.
Do not skip local security review when generated code handles authentication, tokens, or permissions.
Do not apply async patterns blindly to blocking libraries or legacy database drivers.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps design FastAPI services, async data layers, security patterns, tests, observability, and deployment plans.

faq.question: Does it write runnable code?
faq.answer: It can help draft code and plans, but you must test everything in your own environment.

faq.question: Which Python stack does it emphasize?
faq.answer: It focuses on FastAPI, Pydantic V2, SQLAlchemy 2.0, async drivers, pytest, Redis, and common deployment tools.

faq.question: Can it help with existing services?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide your current architecture, endpoint goals, errors, or performance symptoms for targeted recommendations.

faq.question: Is it useful for API security?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers JWT, API keys, RBAC, CORS, validation, rate limiting, and security headers.

faq.question: What should I provide before using it?
faq.answer: Provide requirements, data models, traffic expectations, dependencies, database choices, and deployment targets.
